name: Regorafenib (GIST, third-line)

biomarkers.KIT: regorafenib is a multikinase inhibitor with activity against KIT and PDGFRA, used after imatinib and sunitinib failure
biomarkers.note: Regorafenib is the standard third-line TKI for advanced GIST after failure of imatinib and sunitinib (category 1). It also has activity in SDH-deficient GIST. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors, GIST-D, and DeVita 12th ed. (lines 118434 to 118437).

lineOfTherapy: third-line for unresectable/recurrent/metastatic GIST after failure of imatinib and sunitinib (category 1)

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: disease progression after both imatinib and sunitinib
eligibilityCriteria.locator: lines 118434 to 118437 (regorafenib is standard third-line therapy for advanced GIST, effective in patients failing both imatinib and sunitinib); Standard Guidelines (NCCN) GIST v1.2026, GIST-D (Regorafenib, category 1)

drugs.name: Regorafenib

provenance.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
provenance.locator: lines 118434 to 118437 (regorafenib given 160 mg by mouth daily for 3 weeks every 4 weeks, effective as third-line therapy in patients failing both imatinib and sunitinib, GRID trial)

drugs.notes: Source: DeVita 12th ed. (lines 118434 to 118437, GRID trial). Regorafenib 160 mg PO once daily for 3 weeks (days 1 to 21) followed by a 1-week rest, in a 4-week (28-day) cycle. Days array encodes the 21 on-treatment days of the 28-day cycle. No ISMP tall-man form. Regorafenib-specific monitoring: hypertension (blood pressure), hand-foot skin reaction, hepatotoxicity (LFTs, including a boxed hepatotoxicity warning), fatigue, and diarrhea.

supportiveCare: 160 mg daily for 3 weeks on / 1 week off (28-day cycle); continue until progression or intolerance.
Monitor blood pressure and liver function; assess hand-foot skin reaction each cycle.
Antiemetic/G-CSF prophylaxis not routinely required for oral regorafenib monotherapy.

monitoring: liver function tests (regorafenib hepatotoxicity, boxed warning) - baseline and during first cycles
blood pressure (TKI-associated hypertension) at baseline and each cycle
hand-foot skin reaction assessment each cycle

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 3-4 hand-foot skin reaction, hypertension, or hepatotoxicity
doseModificationRules.text: Hold and resume at a reduced dose (e.g., 120 mg then 80 mg) per labeling; monitor LFTs closely; obtain clinical review.

core.source: DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 12th ed.
core.locator: lines 118434 to 118437 (regorafenib 160 mg by mouth daily for 3 weeks every 4 weeks, third-line GIST, GRID)

guideline.locator: GIST-D 1 of 2 (Regorafenib, category 1, third-line after imatinib and sunitinib); gist lines 1777, 1801

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for regorafenib in GIST (disease #29), third-line after imatinib and sunitinib. Regorafenib 160 mg PO once daily for 3 weeks every 4 weeks is dose-grounded to DeVita 12th ed. (lines 118434 to 118437, GRID trial). Third-line positioning after both imatinib and sunitinib is source-stated (DeVita line 118434; NCCN GIST v1.2026 GIST-D). The GIST NCCN extract confirms regorafenib as a category 1 third-line option but does not print an explicit mg dose, so the concrete 160 mg 3-weeks-on/1-week-off schedule is carried from the DeVita core layer. No dose was invented or inferred and no field is set to VERIFY. This remains a StewardMD Standard Protocol; no endorsement implied.
